comment: Ordered rebrand rules for the openobserve-sdk-android fork (base: UPSTREAM_BASE = dd-sdk-android 3.10.0, matching the version the RN bridge pins). Unlike the RN fork there is NO ours-vs-upstream ambiguity here: the ENTIRE tree IS the SDK being rebranded, so Datadog identifiers are renamed uniformly. Two mechanics are involved: (1) 'content' rules rewrite file text; (2) 'pathRenames' move directories/files (the Kotlin package namespace com/datadog/android and the dd-sdk-android-* module dirs). rebrand.mjs applies pathRenames (git mv) FIRST, then content rules. Order within each list is most-specific-first. Third-party deps (okhttp, kotlin stdlib, PLCrashReporter, gson, etc.) are not Datadog-prefixed and are left alone.

pathRenames.why: Gradle Module Metadata signature dirs (src/main/resources/META-INF/com/datadoghq/dd-sdk-android-*/verification.properties) encode the Maven group as a path. MUST run before com/datadog (which does not match com/datadoghq due to the hq boundary, but explicit-first keeps intent clear).

Kotlin/Java package namespace directory move for ALL com.datadog.* sub-namespaces, not just android: com/datadog/{android,trace,benchmark,tools,gradle,sample,opentelemetry,exec}. Applied as a git mv of each matching <prefix>/com/datadog dir (nested-under-same-rule moves are carried by the parent git mv).

Maven module directory names (32 dirs: dd-sdk-android-core, features/dd-sdk-android-rum, integrations/dd-sdk-android-okhttp, ...) become the published artifact ids. Published Maven coordinate. Uses o2- (not oo-) to match the browser-sdk, which ships o2-api-key/o2source/o2-request-id in production (browser-core intakeSites.ts + endpointBuilder.ts). The mobile forks had drifted to oo-, leaving two different shorthands for the same vendor across the same backend. Note src/api_management/src/auth/validator.rs calls o2-api-key the 'legacy' alias, but legacy-in-the-validator is still what the shipped browser SDK sends, so o2- is the convention with real traffic behind it.

fileRenames.why: class-name FILES whose basename still carries the Datadog token after content rules renamed the class inside them (DatadogLogGenerator.kt -> OpenObserveLogGenerator.kt, DatadogRumMonitorTest.kt, DatadogSiteExtensions.kt, ...). 158 files. Applied as git mv on the basename only (dir segments were handled by pathRenames), after Phase 1 so paths are final.
NDK native source file datadog-ndk.cpp -> openobserve-ndk.cpp (its CMake target + loader refs are handled by the datadog-ndk content rule).

ABI-validator dump FILES named api/dd-sdk-android-<module>.api (the module DIR was moved by the dd-sdk-android- prefix pathRename, but the .api filename basename is a separate token). Aligns the .api file names with the renamed modules.

rules.why: BUILD-BREAKING. GenerateCompilerMetaTask picks a representative class file by requiring its PATH to contain the vendor token, to skip dependencies' classes. The rebrand renames the package to com/openobserve/, so after a sync this filter matches ZERO files, firstOrNull() returns null and checkNotNull throws: 'Couldn't find any class file to get compilation metadata'. It fails `./gradlew assembleLibrariesDebug` on every module. Invisible to every other rule (bare lowercase 'datadog' with no word boundary, uppercase letter or 'hq' suffix) and invisible to check-no-datadog.sh, which does not scan buildSrc — the same blind spot that shipped the NTP hosts, "dd.configuration" and the dd= tracestate key. Scoped to the full expression, not the bare token, so it cannot touch the datadog/trace/** paths in clone_dd_trace.gradle.kts, which are EXTERNAL coordinates in the upstream dd-trace-java repo and must stay verbatim or the clone 404s.

Gradle task GROUP label — the heading these tasks appear under in `./gradlew tasks`. Cosmetic, not shipped, but it is upstream identity visible to every developer who runs Gradle. 11 occurrences across buildSrc. Same bare-lowercase blind spot as the filter above; scoped to the assignment expression so it cannot reach the external datadog/trace/** clone paths.
repo URLs in build files / docs (before the dd-sdk-android artifact rule)
Maven group id in publishing config + build.gradle dependency coordinates
KDoc @see links to Datadog docs (must precede the bare datadoghq.com rule)
residual doc/host URLs in comments + prose

SLASH form of the Maven group (com/datadoghq/dd-java-agent, dd-trace-java in CI/benchmark URLs + KDoc). MUST precede the broad com/datadog slash rule so com/datadoghq is consumed first and never corrupted to com/openobservehq.

SLASH form of the package path for ALL com.datadog.* namespaces (not caught by the dotted com.datadog rule): appears in .api ABI-validator dumps, JNI class descriptors, and test view-URL string assertions (hasViewUrl("com/datadog/android/...")). Must match the pathRenames dir move or those tests fail and apiCheck diverges.

artifact ids + settings.gradle include(':dd-sdk-android-*') + module refs (after the repo-URL rule so it doesn't corrupt it) Published Maven coordinate. The mobile forks had drifted to oo-, leaving two different shorthands for the same vendor across the same backend. package + import declarations across all .kt/.java for ALL com.datadog.* namespaces (android, trace, benchmark, tools, gradle, sample, opentelemetry). Runs AFTER com.datadoghq so the Maven group (com.datadoghq, a superstring) is consumed first and never corrupted to com.openobservehq.
JNI native symbol names in the NDK module's C/C++ (underscore form of the package) — must match the package rename or native crash capture fails to link

public API types/objects AND mid-word compounds: DatadogSite, DatadogInterceptor, getDatadogContext, mapToDatadogTracer. No leading \b so mid-identifier occurrences (getDatadogContext) are caught, not just word-initial ones.

catch-all for any remaining mixed-case Datadog substring (bare entrypoint object, trailing-position Datadog like getDatadog). Runs after the Datadog<Suffix> compound rule. Safe as a plain substring: no token we keep contains 'Datadog' (upstream attribution lives in NOTICE/LICENSE, excluded from the codemod).

lowercase camelCase identifiers (variables, params, properties) not caught by the uppercase-D Datadog<Suffix> rule: datadogContext -> ooContext, datadogTags -> ooTags, datadogCore -> ooCore, datadogSpan/Tracer. Word-boundary guarded so it never matches inside x-datadog-* wire header VALUES (those are followed by '-', not [A-Z]).

SCREAMING_CASE constant NAMES incl. mid-word (DATADOG_INITIAL_CONTEXT, TAG_DATADOG_UPLOAD, DATADOG_EVENT_BRIDGE_NAME). Plain literal so mid-token (after '_') occurrences are caught. Matches the uppercase identifier only; the lowercase x-datadog-* string VALUES those constants hold are a separate wire concern (distributed trace excluded from v1).

the NDK native LIBRARY name: CMake target -> libopenobserve-ndk.so, System.loadLibrary("datadog-ndk"), and the datadog-ndk.cpp source. Ships in the AAR, so it must not carry 'datadog'. Literal so target/loader/JNI stay consistent (also covers datadog-ndk-sample / -test module names).

snake_case identifiers/resources incl. NDK C symbols (datadog_sigaction, datadog_initial_context, datadog_shutdown) and resource names (datadog_violet, datadog_widget). Literal so C symbol definitions AND references rename together (consistency). Does not touch x-datadog-* wire headers (hyphen, not underscore).
residual brand token in comments/handles not ending in .com (the datadoghq.com URL rule ran earlier). e.g. @datadoghq handles, doc references.

DogStatsD (Datadog's StatsD) config-key names in the vendored trace-internal lib (dogstatsd.host/port/...). Not a network call, but carries the Datadog brand; renamed for strict zero-Datadog. Config keys rename consistently (definition + readers use the same constant).
uppercase constant-name form (DOGSTATSD_HOST, DOGSTATSD_PORT, ...)
REQ#1 fail-closed: the STAGING intake host browser-intake-datad0g.com (Datadog staging) -> non-Datadog. Not caught by the datadoghq rule (datad0g uses a zero).

REQ#1 fail-closed: US1_FED/US2_FED intake hosts browser-intake-ddog-gov.com (Datadog FedRAMP) -> non-Datadog. So no OpenObserveSite value can construct a Datadog host; combined with the RN customEndpoint, not a single request can reach Datadog.
REQ#2 wire prefix: RequestFactory QUERY_PARAM_SOURCE (?ddsource=) + log source field. So captured data is OpenObserve-prefixed on the wire.
REQ#2: uppercase constant form of the source token
REQ#2 wire prefix: RequestFactory QUERY_PARAM_TAGS (?ddtags=), the log/rum JSON schema `ddtags` field, and LogEventSerializer. Backend reads ootags/o2tags (doc 02).
REQ#2: uppercase constant form (DDTAGS_KEY_NAME)

AUTH HEADER ONLY. The intake auth key is the single wire token aligned to the browser-sdk's o2- spelling; every other wire key (ootags, oosource, _oo, the oo= tracestate vendor key, oo-client-token, oo-application-id) deliberately stays oo- because those already shipped in alpha1-3 and renaming them again churns the wire for no gain. Ordered BEFORE the broad \bDD-/\bdd- rules so those never see it: once DD-API-KEY becomes O2-API-KEY there is no DD- left to match. Backend takes either spelling - validator.rs extract_rum_token checks oo-api-key then falls back to o2-api-key, in both the query param and the header, and HTTP header names are case-insensitive so O2-API-KEY matches o2-api-key.

REQ#2 wire prefix: intake HTTP header NAMES (DD-API-KEY, DD-EVP-ORIGIN, DD-EVP-ORIGIN-VERSION, DD-REQUEST-ID, DD-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY). HTTP headers are case-insensitive, so OO-API-KEY still matches the backend's oo-api-key (doc 02). \b guards ADD-/ODD-.

REQ#2 wire prefix: lowercase intake header names dd-client-token, dd-application-id -> oo-*. \b guards add-/odd-; dd-sdk-android was already renamed earlier. Does not touch x-datadog-* (that's datadog-, not dd-).

The _dd telemetry namespace (schema key -> _o2 by the _dd rule) drives json2kotlin to generate the Kotlin types O2/O2Device/O2Session and property o2. Its CONSUMERS must match those generated names. These namespace types are split out here, BEFORE the general \bDd([A-Z]) -> Oo rule, because that rule is overloaded: it also renames the public classes DdRumContentProvider/DdProfilingContentProvider/DdSpan (which stay Oo* until the identifier rename). Oo/OoDevice/OoSession never collide with those class names.

the schema `_dd`->`_oo` rename regenerates the event models' nested classes as Oo* (OoSession, OoDevice, ...). The hand-written scopes/generators reference the OLD Dd* names (ErrorEvent.DdSession, LogEvent.DdDevice) + the DdRumContentProvider auto-init class -> Oo*. Boundary-guarded so it never matches mid-identifier.

bare generated nested class `.Dd` (LogEvent.Dd(, ErrorEvent.Dd(, ...) -> `.Oo` to match the regenerated `_oo` model. Not caught by the Dd<Suffix> rule (Dd is followed by '(' not [A-Z]). RETARGETED .Oo->.O2 for the _o2 namespace member access.

the event models' `_dd`->`_oo` field is the named constructor arg `dd = <Event>.Dd(...)` in every RUM/log scope + telemetry handler -> `oo = `. All `dd = ` occurrences in shipped source are this model arg. RETARGETED oo=->o2= : the _o2 namespace named argument / local-var declaration.

property access on the event models' renamed field: `event.dd.copy(...)`, `.dd.documentVersion`, `element.dd` -> `.oo`. Matches the regenerated `val oo: Oo` property. RETARGETED .oo->.o2 for the _o2 namespace property access.
internal telemetry namespace field (matches the schema fork)
session-replay privacy resource ids (datadog_hidden, datadog_image_privacy, ...) — rename resource + refs

W3C TRACESTATE vendor key. Wire-visible on EVERY traced request, and on the DEFAULT path since tracecontext became the default propagator — so removing the proprietary propagator swapped one upstream identifier on the wire for another. Invisible to every other rule (bare lowercase, no word boundary), which is the same blind spot that shipped the NTP hosts. All three SDKs had to move together or trace linking breaks between them; the backend stores trace_state opaquely and does not parse the key, so nothing server-side is affected.

openQuestions.Q3_package_root: com.openobserve.android chosen (mirrors com.datadog.android; Maven group is ai.openobserve reverse-DNS). Confirm before publishing.
openQuestions.Q4_module_scope: The RN bridge (3.5.3) imports rum, logs, trace, webview, ndk, flags (+ transitive core) at 3.10.0 — NOT okhttp. Doc 01 wanted to EXCLUDE trace + flags. To keep the RN bridge compiling unchanged we must fork+publish everything it imports (incl. trace/webview/flags). Alternative: strip trace/webview/flags usage from the RN bridge. Default: fork what the bridge needs; disable the features at the JS layer, not by removing native modules.
